coupling: The earlier commit narrows the accumulated string-table byte count to 16 bits while retaining each string’s individual bounds check, so oversized sums remain safely rejected. The later commit removes that per-string check because the aggregate table-size check appears to cover every string. Together, two encoded 32768-byte lengths wrap the aggregate count to zero, and the first string construction reads beyond the supplied metadata. A fix must restore a nonwrapping aggregate bound or retain an independent per-string bound; reviewing either edit without the other misses the unsafe assumption.
